## Our Research

The Winter Lab studies infectious disease dynamics and population immunity to inform prevention, surveillance, control, and elimination. Led by Dr. Amy Winter, Associate Professor in the Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics at the University of Georgia, our work is united by **policy-driven science**: we partner directly with policymakers to shape research questions and build the methodological tools needed to answer them rigorously.

Our research connects transmission and intervention modelling, prediction and surveillance, and population immunity and seroepidemiology. We use mathematical models, statistics, machine learning, simulation, and field data to study questions across pathogens and settings. Measles, rubella, and other vaccine-preventable infections remain major areas of work, while the lab's questions and methods extend more broadly across infectious disease epidemiology. We work in close collaboration with the World Health Organization, The Gates Foundation, Gavi the Vaccine Alliance, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, Pennsylvania State University, colleagues across UGA, and in-country partners in Zambia.

## Join the Lab

We welcome graduate students and postdoctoral fellows interested in infectious disease epidemiology and quantitative public health research. Lab members may work with mathematical modelling, statistical methods, machine learning, serological data, surveillance data, or applied biostatistics. Students develop strong quantitative skills while contributing to projects with direct public health relevance. If you are interested in joining, please reach out to Amy at [awinter@uga.edu](mailto:awinter@uga.edu).

:::
